To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a linear stability analysis of the mixed-boundary-condition, stochastically forced, thermally dominant mean-state box model yields a single damped oscillatory thermohaline mode in addition to damped purely thermally driven modes; (2) the variability of the model in response to a moderate amount of atmospheric stochastic forcing is dominated by this mode; and (3) the model's variability shares many features with that of a coupled ocean-atmosphere general circulation model.
the stochastic atmospheric forcing in our model is responsible for the oscillatory variability in the coupled model.

(1) the interdecadal variability in the coupled model is primarily driven by stochastic atmospheric forcing, and (2) a four-box linear ocean model with a stochastic atmospheric forcing is sufficient to describe qualitatively the variability of the coupled model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interdecadal variability in an idealized coupled model of the atmosphere–ocean system.
a linear model of the thermohaline overturning circulation of the ocean.
the study of a linear model of the ocean's THC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stochastic forcing of the oceanic THC in the box model, which is a simplified representation of the coupled ocean– atmosphere THC, is a useful tool to understand some aspects of the interdecadal THC variations in the coupled GCM.
the linear oscillator model is a useful and simple tool to understand some of the features of interdecadal variability.
a linear oscillator driven by stochastic forcing is capable of producing interdecadal variability that has many qualitative aspects of that found in a fully nonlinear coupled model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a linear model that is capable of capturing the main aspects of the interdecadal variability in a coupled GCM, and we have provided a simple explanation for the mechanism responsible for the variability.
the linear thermohaline oscillatory mode is a useful concept for understanding the interdecadal variability in the coupled GCM.
the linear oscillator is an effective and efficient model for describing the interdecadal THC oscillations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stochastic forcing of the oceanic THC can be described as a linear thermohaline oscillator driven by stochastic atmospheric forcing.
the stochastic forcing of an unstable system can lead to the same kind of variability as the forcing of a stable system by an unstable mode.

stochastic forcing can be used to drive interdecadal variability in a simple linear box model, and that this variability has many common features to the variability in a coupled ocean–atmo-sphere GCM.
